limitations: Code simulation does not establish board-level timing.
Proposed FPGA logic and timing figures are conceptual; no hardware measurements are claimed.
No synthesis resource usage, power or Fmax benchmark is asserted.
UART, SPI and I2C examples are intentionally scoped teaching units, not production protocol IP.
Chapter 14 STA numbers are arithmetic examples, not measured or Vivado-reported slack.
Chapter 15 Tcl is a guarded demonstration; no vendor build or board programming is claimed.
Chapter 16 Quartus project is generic; no board-specific pin assignment or Quartus compilation is claimed.
Chapter 17 Questa run.do is provided but public CI runs Icarus; no Questa license or simulation run is claimed.
Chapter 19 AXI4-Lite subordinate is 32-bit and single-outstanding; it is not a full AXI4 interconnect or DMA.
Chapter 20 MicroBlaze V block design is a system contract and firmware example; no board-specific XSA, ELF, bitstream or hardware run is claimed.
Build Manifest hashes input files but does not guarantee identical bitstreams across tool versions, seeds or machine environments.
Chapter 18 explains IP packaging and system integration contracts but does not claim that the sample AXI peripheral has been packaged into a vendor-specific IP archive.
Chapter 21 tests RV32I immediate generation and hazard-control helpers only; it is not a complete CPU or ISA-certified implementation.
Chapter 22 calculator covers NRZ line coding ratios and a user-supplied protocol factor; it does not model PAM4/FEC, PCIe packet overhead or real SerDes behavior.
Chapter 23 includes a synchronous event counter; no ILA/SignalTap hardware capture was performed.
Chapter 24 CI checks the iCEstick flow statically; no Yosys/nextpnr bitstream build, programmer run or board test is claimed.
Chapter 25 timing/power calculators are mathematical teaching aids; no vendor STA engine, implementation report or device power measurement was run.
The nextpnr support table is a snapshot; the Nexus backend is experimental/alpha, and NanoXplore NG-Ultra binary bitstream generation requires proprietary Impulse.
Chapter 26 FIR4 C++ test checks arithmetic and state, not actual Vitis HLS scheduling/II, RTL co-simulation, FPGA resources or timing.
Chapter 27 ready_valid_slice test checks one synchronous 16-bit instance under deterministic backpressure; it is not an AXI CDC FIFO, exhaustive formal proof or PPA measurement.

Chapter 28 synthetic three-frame RGB threshold core does not implement camera PHY, DDR controller, DMA, CDC, Sobel, display timing or board-level operation; bandwidth script gives active-pixel lower bounds.
